overview: Black counterattacks with 2...f5, and after 3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4 6.Nc3 Qg6 White keeps the extra pawn and a sound centre while Black has open f-file and quick development hoping for traps. White is better with accurate play, and 3.d3 is a calmer try. Strong players consider it unsound.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with 3.Nxe5, answer ...Qf6 with d4 and Nc4, then consolidate with Nc3
Avoid the traps (3.Nxe5 Qf6 4.d4 d6 5.Nc4 fxe4 6.Nc3 Qg6 7.Ne3) and keep the extra pawn

black_ideas.idea: Use the open f-file and quick development for an attack against the white king
Set tactical traps with ...Qf6 and ...Qxe5-type tactics or ...Bc5 and ...Nf6

typical_structures.structure: White extra pawn in the centre; Black weakened kingside with an open f-file

character.notes: Counter-gambit with early queen sorties and traps; one slip loses quickly.

gambit.notes: White can keep the e5 pawn.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound by strong players; scores on surprise.

structure.notes: Open centre with the f-file and e-file in play.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.notes: Black needs to know the traps; a dubious line is never beginner.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.d3
sublines_that_differ.how: Declines the pawn and plays a quiet Philidor-type game.

character.reason: Counter-gambit with early queen play and mutual attacks.

gambit.reason: Black gives the e5 pawn and White can keep it.

level.reason: Knowing the traps matters; dubious so not beginner.

plans.reason: Black uses the queen early and develops quickly for the pawn.
